865.t: His father's playing and early death
865.s: His father played jazz, dance and brass bands, and accordion, and died about 1906-07 when Bill was small. The name of the father is discussed.
865.q: Well he didn't have no special bands. Yeah, he used to play jazz. And also he used to be an accordion player, you know. Accordion.

865.t: Father's cornet and the family photograph
865.s: Phillips recalls his father's brass cornet and says a sister has a photograph the interviewers hope to copy.
865.q: No, my sister, one of my sisters have it. That would be wonderful. We could find that stuff and make a copy of it. I'd like to find it myself.

174.t: Burnell's looks and the musical Santiago family
174.s: Burnell's size and color, and how the Santiago siblings learned piano from one another without lessons.
174.q: Well I don't think he took lessons. I think they played piano like this. You see the older brother Harold Santiago used to play piano. And that's their, uh. Their uncle Willie.

999.t: His father, William Jones, played cornet
999.s: His father played B-flat cornet, studied at Xavier, and played with Thomas Coleman; Allen asks for his address to interview him.
999.q: Yeah well my father He played the cornet I hear him talk about it a lot of the time So he played B flat cornet He used to go to Xavier's school Up here on St. Charles Street That's where he was He finished school at You know He had a little outfit down to cut off They used to play with the band…

430.t: His uncle Louis Arthidore and his father in the Onward Brass Band
430.s: His uncle was a fine clarinetist; his father played cornet then alto in the same brass band.
430.q: Well, my uncle, my mother's brother, he was one of the finest clarinetists we had here in New Orleans, I understand. What I was told from a lot of old time musicians, his name was Louis Arthedale, and he played with the Armored Brass Band, it was many, many years ago. My father happened to be in…

8.t: Older brother John Garland and his instruments
8.s: His older brother John, now ill in Philadelphia, played violin, trombone, mandolin and guitar; only he and Ed survive.
8.q: Is he still living? That's what I'm telling you about. That's what I don't know. I just mail, fixed the mail of that again. I got a letter from him saying he was very little sick, you know, in Philadelphia. 642 North 47th Street, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. And I haven't gotten no answer. That's…

762.t: Gaspar's, the opera conductor, and his unrecorded family of musicians
762.s: Playing intermission at Gaspar's, he saw the friend astonish an opera conductor; he never recorded, from a musical family.
762.q: I worked in intermission. I was playing intermission for him at Gaspar's on Bourbon Street. And they had an opera at one of the places in New Orleans. And the conductor came after. And Gaspar knew Bourbon, the man who owned the place was Gaspar. He knew Bourbon could play. And he came up and told…

629.t: His younger brother Euless, singer and composer
629.s: Picou describes his younger brother as a good singer and composer of French and Creole songs who played guitar; he taught him.
629.q: ah my brother used to sing he was a good singer wasn't he i never knew him he was a great talent what was his name and his name euless euless euless was he older or younger than you oh he was younger than me younger about how much younger was he about four years about four years about something…

121.s: Aunts Pauline and Nancy and Uncle Buddy sang; his mother and brother Louis did not.
121.q: No. You know what, my mama was, yeah. My mama wasn't much of a singer. My aunt, Pauline was a singer. My aunt, Toot, her other sister. Aunt Toot was a, her name was Nancy. And Pauline and Uncle Buddy was a singer. But my mama was, you know, there was always one in the family that didn't sing to.…

404.t: Harold's cousin Johnny Brunious and Harold's family
404.s: Harold talks about his first cousin Johnny Brunious (Slack Loon Johnny), a New York trip in 1936, and his mother's Planchard family.
404.q: that was still it was it was a little past the 20s on the 30s yeah yeah yeah that's right my daddy my uncle my cousin because my my cousin uh we used to call him sly con johnny that's my that's my first cousin yeah yeah what was that was there was that's no no that's a burnis they were johnny…

886.t: Brother Bill Casimir, cousin Sam and family in Chicago
886.s: Casimir talks about his brother and first cousin, musicians who played with Walter Pichon and Natty Dominique's band in Chicago and on records.
886.q: Yeah, my brother was playing. Bill Kazma, one of the best talent players they had. He used to go to Walter Pichon on the boat. And uh, quite a lot of you out there, they go playing every night. I'm not playing. Bill Kazma, they played a ton of slacks.

118.t: The Frasier family and piano styles
118.s: His grandfather's family from Seabrook: Alec and Mitchell Frasier, their piano style, and Lil Frank Moyer.
118.q: Yeah, but all that's sick with Seabrook. That's where the biggest portion of my family comes from, on my grandfather's side, the Frasiers. Great piano player like Mitchell Frasier, Alec Frasier. Alec Frasier? Yeah.

108.t: Wilder's father, a bassist into his late eighties
108.s: His father played cornet, sousaphone and bass violin, played until 88, and turned 95.
108.q: My father played, originally cornet and then he switched to sousaphone and while he was playing sousaphone he studied bass violin and so he doubled on sousaphone and bass violin when that was in vogue, and then later on he just played bass violin. And my father played I guess until he was about 87,…
